title: Your AI remembers you. Can it remember a lie?
subtitle: What happens when a remembered claim becomes permission to act
description: Follow a false approval across sessions, inspect 40 synthetic memory-authority episodes, and see why provenance and current permission need separate checks.
evidence: Synthetic cross-session example; no model calls

title: Testing subscription abuse at the action boundary
subtitle: Evaluate cancellations, refunds, and paid access through their actual effects
description: A synthetic subscription workflow compares permissions, business invariants, and deny-all controls, with recorded effects, explicit completion limits, and replayable evidence.

title: Designing an Evidence Trail for Agent Actions
subtitle: Connecting requests, policy decisions, execution, and observed state
description: I trace one synthetic agent action from its request to its observed effect, then examine what event hashes, snapshots, and replay can establish—and what needs additional verification.

title: When rules beat decision models
subtitle: Lessons from an executed tool-selection evaluation
description: I replaced a label-matching diagnostic with an executable support workflow. On 144 synthetic test episodes, the rules baseline outperformed the tested zero-shot model configurations.
